evidence.title: Masatoshi Ichikawa
evidence.text: Masatoshi Ichikawa (市川 雅敏 , Ichikawa Masatoshi , born 11 January 1961, in Tokyo) was a pioneering Japanese professional racing cyclist.

evidence.title: Masatoshi Ichikawa
evidence.text: He was the first Japanese to ride professionally in Europe, riding for such teams as the Belgian team Hitachi and the Swiss team Bleiker in the late 1980s and early 1990s.

evidence.title: Masatoshi Ichikawa
evidence.text: He was also the first to complete a Grand Tour event, finishing 50th in the Giro d'Italia in 1990.

evidence.title: Al-Karaji
evidence.text: Abū Bakr ibn Muḥammad ibn al Ḥusayn al-Karajī (c. 953 – c. 1029) was a 10th-century Persian mathematician and engineer who flourished at Baghdad.

evidence.title: Al-Karaji
evidence.text: He was born in Karaj, a city near Tehran.

evidence.title: Al-Karaji
evidence.text: His three principal surviving works are mathematical: "Al-Badi' fi'l-hisab" ("Wonderful on calculation"), "Al-Fakhri fi'l-jabr wa'l-muqabala" ("Glorious on algebra"), and "Al-Kafi fi'l-hisab" ("Sufficient on calculation").

evidence.title: Masatoshi Shima
evidence.text: Masatoshi Shima (嶋 正利 , Shima Masatoshi , born August 22, 1943, Shizuoka) is a Japanese electronics engineer, who was one of the designers of the world's first microprocessor, the Intel 4004, along with Federico Faggin, Ted Hoff, and Stanley Mazor.

evidence.title: Masatoshi Ishida
evidence.text: Masatoshi Ishida (石田 真敏 , Ishida Masatoshi , born April 11, 1952) is a Japanese politician of the Liberal Democratic Party, a member of the House of Representatives in the Diet (national legislature).

evidence.title: Masatoshi Ishida
evidence.text: A native of Kainan, Wakayama and graduate of Waseda University, he was elected to the first of his three terms in the assembly of Wakayama Prefecture in 1983 and then to the first of his two terms as mayor of Kainan in 1994.

evidence.title: Masatoshi Ishida
evidence.text: He was elected to the House of Representatives for the first time in 2002.

evidence.title: Masatoshi Ono
evidence.text: Masatoshi Ono (小野正利 , Ono Masatoshi , born January 29, 1967 in Adachi, Tokyo, Japan) , also known as Sho, is a Japanese rock/heavy metal singer-songwriter and vocal coach.

evidence.title: Masatoshi Ono
evidence.text: Ono got his start in the 1980s as vocalist of the heavy metal band Fort Bragg.

evidence.title: Masatoshi Ono
evidence.text: In 1992, he released his first solo single, "Pure ni Nare", on Sony Records.

evidence.title: Masatoshi Ono
evidence.text: But it wasn't until his third single, "You're the Only...", that he hit it big.

evidence.title: Masatoshi Ono
evidence.text: The single helped Ono win the "Rookie of the Year" award at the 34th Japan Record Awards and an invitation to that year's "Kōhaku Uta Gassen".

evidence.title: Motohisa Ikeda
evidence.text: Motohisa Ikeda (池田 元久 , Ikeda Motohisa , born December 20, 1940) is a Japanese politician of the Democratic Party of Japan, a member of the House of Representatives in the Diet (national legislature).

evidence.title: Motohisa Ikeda
evidence.text: A native of Fujisawa, Kanagawa and graduate of Waseda University, he worked at the public broadcaster NHK as a reporter from 1964 to 1989.

evidence.title: Motohisa Ikeda
evidence.text: He was elected to the House of Representatives for the first time in 1990 as a member of the Japan Socialist Party but lost his seat in 1993.

evidence.title: Motohisa Ikeda
evidence.text: He was re-elected in 1996

evidence.title: Augustine of Canterbury
evidence.text: Augustine of Canterbury (born first third of the 6th century – died probably 26 May 604) was a Catholic Benedictine monk who became the first Archbishop of Canterbury in the year 597.

evidence.title: Augustine of Canterbury
evidence.text: He is considered the "Apostle to the English" and a founder of the Catholic Church in England.

evidence.title: Masatoshi Gündüz Ikeda
evidence.text: Masatoşi Gündüz İkeda (Japanese: 池田 正敏 ギュンドゥズ Ikeda Masatoshi Gyunduzu ) (25 February 1926 – 9 February 2003), was a Turkish mathematician of Japanese ancestry, known for his contributions to the field of algebraic number theory.

evidence.title: Despoina
evidence.text: In Greek mythology, Despoina, Despoena or Despoine, was the daughter of Demeter and Poseidon and sister of Arion.

evidence.title: Despoina
evidence.text: She was the goddess of mysteries of Arcadian cults worshipped under the title "Despoina", "the mistress" alongside her mother Demeter, one of the goddesses of the Eleusinian mysteries.

evidence.title: Despoina
evidence.text: Her real name could not be revealed to anyone except those initiated to her mysteries.

evidence.title: Despoina
evidence.text: Pausanias spoke of Demeter as having two daughters; Kore being born first, then later Despoina.

evidence.title: Despoina
evidence.text: With Zeus being the father of Kore, and Poseidon as the father of Despoina.

evidence.title: Despoina
evidence.text: Pausanias made it clear that Kore is Persephone, though he wouldn't reveal Despoina's proper name.
